question: Does the harmonized record track physical burned area, and is the 2012 jump an instrument change?

source.name: NASA MCD64A1 Collection 6.1 burned area (Burn_Date)
source.licence: NASA data are openly available; cite the LP DAAC and the MCD64A1 product team

method.burned_area: MCD64A1 C6.1 Burn_Date > 0 pixels inside the area bbox, 500 m sinusoidal grid
method.compared: harmonized Aqua-scale hotspots per km2 and raw all-sensor detections per km2
method.correlation: Spearman rho over the monthly series (average ranks for ties)
method.step_test: mean of the twelve calendar months of 2012 against the same months of 2009, 2010, 2011
method.partial_months: months the publisher marked partial are excluded

limitations: The Planetary Computer mirror is missing a few MCD64A1 product months (2023-09 and 2024-07 for most areas); those months are listed in catalogue_gaps and left out of the comparison.
Burned area measures physical extent, not detections: one large burn and many small burns give the same hotspot count but very different burned area.
MCD64A1 is itself a MODIS change-detection product, so it shares MODIS's view of what burns and misses small and agricultural fires.
Detection counts also depend on cloud, smoke and overpass geometry, which burned area does not.
A correlation between two monthly series is evidence of agreement, not proof that either counts fires, and burned area is not a fire perimeter.

The 2012 step compares 2012 with 2009–2011 in the same calendar months. An exceptional year in the baseline moves that ratio a long way (Alberta's 2011), which is why the median across areas is the number to read, not the per-area one.
